text: A report page should make one point clearly, not show off every chart type you know. Here's how to keep it honest while you're at it.

A handful of choices genuinely distort a comparison: 3D effects and axes that don't start at zero both exaggerate differences. Pie charts lose their point past a small number of slices — humans compare bar lengths far better than angles. And mixing a measure in the millions with one in the thousands, on the same axis, flattens the smaller one completely.

Keep displayed numbers to three or four significant digits. And sorting isn't just tidiness — sort by measure to highlight extremes, sort by category to help someone find a specific item. Same chart, same data, different story depending on which you choose.

Look again at this dashboard: consistent color, consistent scale, and a treemap where size itself does the sorting. Every one of these is a small, deliberate storytelling decision — not a default left untouched.
Last lesson of the chapter: putting everything together into one professional executive dashboard, start to finish.
